s1.syndrome_frame: short stature with skeletal abnormalities and distinctive facial features
salient_findings: distinctive facial features including frontal bossing and micrognathia
skeletal abnormalities including diffuse osteosclerosis and acro-osteolysis
key_facts: short terminal phalanges with bulbous fingertips present
normal cardiovascular, respiratory, abdominal, and neurologic examinations
normal serum calcium, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase, vitamin D level, thyroid function, and insulin-like growth factor 1
skeletal survey showed diffuse osteosclerosis, biconvex vertebrae, a wide open anterior fontanel with Wormian bones, and acro-osteolysis of the distal phalanges

shortlist.label: Pycnodysostosis
shortlist.why_kept: diffuse osteosclerosis, acro-osteolysis, and skeletal abnormalities match this condition

shortlist.label: Osteopetrosis
shortlist.why_kept: diffuse osteosclerosis is a key feature of this disease

shortlist.label: Dysosteosclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: skeletal survey findings and short stature are consistent with this rare condition

shortlist.label: Cleidocranial dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: large open anterior fontanel and skeletal abnormalities are features of this disease

shortlist.label: Oculo-dento-osseous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: distinctive facial features and skeletal abnormalities are consistent with this condition

raw.rationale: The combination of short stature, diffuse osteosclerosis, biconvex vertebrae, large open anterior fontanel, micrognathia, and acro-osteolysis of the distal phalanges are characteristic features of Pycnodysostosis.

rejected.label: Osteopetrosis
rejected.why: While osteopetrosis also presents with osteosclerosis, the presence of a large open anterior fontanel and acro-osteolysis are more suggestive of Pycnodysostosis.

rejected.label: Dysosteosclerosis
rejected.why: Dysosteosclerosis typically presents with more severe neurological impairment and a different skeletal survey profile.

rejected.label: Cleidocranial dysplasia
rejected.why: Cleidocranial dysplasia is characterized by the absence or hypoplasia of the clavicles, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Oculo-dento-osseous dysplasia
rejected.why: Oculo-dento-osseous dysplasia primarily affects the eyes, teeth, and bones, with a distinct set of features that do not match the case description.
